headline: Recommended approving longer spray park hours, one day a week, for the 2027 season, as amended.
summary: Members discussed petitions and communications on memorials, parks, playgrounds, lights, wildlife, and a dam. They recommended extending spray park hours by one hour one day a week, as amended. The other items were recommended for filing or for holding.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 15, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Recommended filing the proposed Purple Heart and Gold Star Memorials item, 3-0.
Recommended filing the summer 2026 aquatic program communication, 3-0.
Recommended holding the petition to restore the Arries Ann Ward Playground name at Great Brook Valley, 3-0.
Recommended filing the petition to repair court lights at Morgan Landing, 580 Grove St., 3-0.
Recommended approval, as amended, of extending spray park hours by one hour for one day a week for the 2027 season, 3-0.
Recommended filing the petition to reduce the European Starling population, 3-0.
Recommended holding the petition on deterring wildlife from going over the Salisbury Pond Dam, 3-0.

Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be 
made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official 
emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email 
address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of 
Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your 
specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location . 
The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.

a.

. Communications of the City Manager - Veterans' Services 3 
Transmitting informational communication relative to the proposed Purple Heart and 
Gold Star Memorials at Worcester Common.
# 7c CC June 2, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery, who discussed the selected design and location, as well as the cost , 
funding sources and timeline related to the installation of the Purple Heart and Gold Star 
Memorials.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Director of Veterans Services, who discussed the 
timeline related to the design and installation process of the memorials.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Bilotta, who discussed whether the design of 
the granite podium will include the names of Gold Star Families, the materials of the star and 
heart casts and the location of the memorials with the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and 
Cemetery.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Deputy City Clerk, who discussed the procedural 
motion for the item.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed. 
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Communication of the City Manager - Parks, Recreation and Cemetery 4 
Transmitting informational communication relative to the summer 2026 aquatic program.
# 8.10A CM June 16, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery, who provided an overview of the item, including actions related to the 
city’s aquatic program during the summer of 2026.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Deputy City Clerk, who discussed the procedural 
motion for the item.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed. 
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
October 6, 2026 Page 3 of 8Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation  Committee
. Miscellaneous Items 5 
Petition of Gordon Ward et al. request the playground at Great Brook Valley be returned 
to its original name of "Arries Ann Ward Playground."
# 20a CC June 2, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery, who discussed the Parks Commission hearing associated with the item , 
as well as challenges related to having multiple names apply for the naming of the playground in 
Great Brook Valley. 
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo discussed ways in which the city could name different components 
within Great Brook Valley to honor and recognize both Arries Ann Ward and Roberto Clemente , 
who are both important figures to the neighborhood.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Rivera, who discussed plans to name a park 
and a street after Arries Ann Ward.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery , 
who discussed the existing Roberto Clemente softball field at Great Brook Valley and discussions 
regarding naming the ballpark and two playgrounds located in Great Brook Valley after Roberto 
Clementine and Arries Ann Ward.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Bilotta, who spoke concerning the item.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held.
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
October 6, 2026 Page 4 of 8Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation  Committee
Petition of Patrick Grady request the court lights at Morgan Landing, located at 580 
Grove St., be repaired.
# 10t CC August 18, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery, who provided a recommendation to file the item, as through the City 
Park Master Planning process, the city plans to remove the tennis courts at the location and 
instead install a new tennis court at Indian Lake Beach, thus making the lighting repairs fiscally 
unfeasible in the long term.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Bilotta, who discussed whether the Indian 
Lake Park Master Plan is available on the city’s website, as well as whether there were any 
updates concerning the master plan with the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery. 
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed.
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
October 6, 2026 Page 5 of 8Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation  Committee
Petition of Christina Foley request the city spray park hours of operation for the 2027 
season be extended to provide earlier morning hours.
# 10s CC August 18, 2026
c.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the following Speaker:
1. Christina Foley, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery , 
who discussed operational cost and staffing challenges relative to extending hours for the spray 
parks.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Rivera, who discussed the feasibility of 
shifting the operational hours to provide services earlier in the day and the challenges concerning 
operating the spray parks in a different timeframe to other aquatic facilities and programs with 
the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Bilotta, who discussed staffing for the spray 
parks, how adjusting the hour of operations may affect staff scheduling, the feasibility of adjusting 
the hours of operations for one or two days a week and how the current hours of operation 
accommodate when the temperature is highest in a day with the Commissioner of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery , 
who discussed bringing forth a report on the impact of adjusting the spray parks hours of 
operations for one day a week at the end of the aquatic season.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved to amend the item to read as follows, “Petition of Christina 
Foley request the city spray park hours of operation for the 2027 season be extended by one hour 
for one day a week.”
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: Request City 
Manager request Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery provide City Council with a 
report related to the impact of adjusting the city’s spray parks hours of operation by extending 
the operations by one hour for one day a week.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved as 
amended.
Recommend Approval as Amended on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

Petition of Ilanit Megidesh request efforts be made to reduce the city 's population of the 
invasive bird species know as the European Starling.
# 12o CC September 8, 2026
d.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery, who provided the recommendation for the item to be forwarded to the 
Massachusetts Division of Fisheries and Wildlife (MassWildlife) for review.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Rivera, who discussed concerns related to 
the invasive bird species with the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Bilotta, who spoke concerning the item.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: Request City 
Manager forward a copy of the September 8, 2026 Petition of Ilanit Megidesh related to reducing 
the population of the invasive bird species known as the European Starling to the Massachusetts 
Division of Fisheries and Wildlife (MassWildlife).
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed.
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays

Petition of Maria V. Montano request Institute Pond (a.k.a. Salisbury Pond) be evaluated 
to implement humane and preventative measures to deter wildlife from going over 
Salisbury Pond Dam.
# 8t CC September 22, 2026
e.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Maria Montano, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Commissioner of Public Works, who discussed 
previous methods used by the department to prevent wildlife from entering the Salisbury Pond 
Dam, as well as challenges related to improving upon the current setup within the spillway at the 
location with the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery and Speaker #1.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized Councilor Bilotta, who discussed the feasibility of 
installing a barrier around the top of the hydraulic lip with the Director of Sewer Operations.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Commissioner of Public Works, who discussed the 
installation of a camera at Salisbury Pond to watch and study the wildlife with Speaker #1.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo recognized the Deputy City Clerk, who discussed the procedural 
motion for the item.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: Request City 
Manager request Commissioner of Public Works provide City Council with an update in six (6) 
months concerning any efforts made to implement and /or improve upon humane and preventative 
measures to deter wildlife from going over the Salisbury Pond Dam.
Chairperson Councilor Fresolo moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
